articles.title: Marlon Humphrey on Ja'Marr Chase: It would be cool if I didn't match up with him so much
articles.summary: Humphrey and Chase have faced off nine times. In those games, Chase has torched the Ravens for 77 catches for 1,245 yards and eight touchdowns.
articles.body:
Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey has covered Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase many times. Maybe more times than he'd like.

Humphrey and Chase have faced off eight times in the regular season and once in the playoffs. In those nine games, Chase has torched the Ravens for 77 catches for 1,245 yards and eight touchdowns.

The Ravens and Bengals will meet again on Sunday, and Humphrey said today that covering Chase and fellow Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is a big challenge, and one of the toughest assignments an NFL cornerback can draw.

"It would be cool if I didn't match up with him so much," Humphrey said. "He's obviously one of the best in the game. Tee is right up there with him, in the Top 10, I think, in this league. There will be plays made, I think the biggest thing going into this matchup is to try to win more than they win and try to limit the explosives. That's the biggest thing when you're guarding those Top 10, Top 5 guys. It's an all-hands-on-deck game. We look forward to the challenge. I think it'll be a great opportunity."

Despite the success Chase has had against him, Humphrey said he's eager for a big game on Sunday between the 4-2 Ravens and 3-2 Bengals.

"I'm very confident. I think we've had some tests this year, but this will be by far the biggest test yet," Humphrey said.

If Chase's past is any indication, it's going to be a very big test for Humphrey and the Ravens' secondary.

articles.title: Giants’ J.J. McCarthy drops game-changing Jaxson Dart revelation as he replaces Jameis Winston
articles.summary: The New York Giants recently announced that JJ McCarthy would be replacing Jameis Winston as the team’s starting quarterback for this week’s game against the...
articles.body:
The New York Giants recently announced that JJ McCarthy would be replacing Jameis Winston as the team's starting quarterback for this week's game against the Houston Texans. The news comes after McCarthy took over for Winston down the stretch of last week's game vs the New Orleans Saints and nearly led the team on a miraculous comeback.

Now, McCarthy has spoken about his relationship with Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart , whose injury opened the door for Winston to become the starter in the first place.

"I talked to him today, just normal conversation. We're both just rooting for each other. And like I told him, I'm doing the same thing that you want, is help win the football games for this organization and do everything we can and be the best versions of ourselves every day to help the collective," he said, per Giants.com.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

McCarthy also spoke on how Dart is helping him out with the X's and O's ahead of his first start in New York.

"It's going to be great because he is such a smart player and obviously very well-rounded in this offense. It's going to be awesome to just ask him really anything and pick his brain about anything," he said.

McCarthy was acquired by the Giants from the Minnesota Vikings earlier this season shortly after Dart's injury, giving New York an insurance policy in case Winston's struggles continued, which they certainly did.

McCarthy overcame an early interception to put up some elite production against the Saints down the stretch on Sunday, nearly pulling off a comeback for the ages in that one.

Now, he'll be matched up against a Texans defense that was arguably the best in the league last year and has now started to round back into form this year.

articles.title: McDermott calls for Super League to accept NRL investment
articles.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott calls for Super League to accept investment from Australia's NRL in order to improve the English game.
articles.body:
England head coach Brian McDermott has called for Super League to accept investment from Australia's NRL in order to improve the English game.

Talks are currently ongoing after Super League clubs rejected a £35m package from the Australian Rugby League Commission and a second deadline of 15 October was allowed to pass without an agreement being reached.

Formalising a partnership between the sport's two leading competitions is seen as as a key step in helping to grow the European competition's revenue.

"I think the NRL's investment in Super League could be very, very positive," said McDermott, who is also the assistant coach of the Gold Coast Titans.

"The product's brilliant. It has always being brilliant. The product's never been the problem. The players have never been the problem. The coaches have never been the problem.

"It's just how it's marketed and how it's presented to people. I think there's some dominoes could start falling our way if the NRL invests and we accept their investment."

Super League is yet to agree a new title sponsorship deal, finalise broadcast negotiations or even its fixtures for the 2027 campaign with London Broncos' position yet to be fully determined.

The Broncos came in16th on the yearly grading list, below fellow Championship side Barrow Raiders, despite a season in which they won the second tier's Grand Final, the 1895 Cup and were runaway champions in the regular-season standings.

The Broncos were overlooked 12 months ago when Bradford Bulls, York Knights and Toulouse Olympique joined the expanded 14-team competition.

But with the backing of Australian businessman Grant Wechsel and former Brisbane Broncos star Darren Lockyer, and with a squad full of internationals, they do still harbour hopes of playing in Super League in 2027.

It is understood any completed deal would involve the Australian governing body insisting on Broncos featuring in the top flight in the near future.

The financial gulf between the northern and southern hemisphere's elite competitions was laid bare, when the NRL struck a record $5.3bn (£3.97bn) television deal over seven years in July.

Super League's TV deal with Sky Sports, which expired at the end of 2026, was worth around £21.5m per year.

"I know there's some positive notes around Super League at the moment, especially with crowds," McDermott added.

"It's been a really interesting competition this year and Wakefield winning the Grand Final puts a brilliant marker down that all the teams can win it.

"It would be a real positive validation of Super League if the NRL were to invest."

McDermott also stressed that an injection of finance into the English game would help widen the pool of talent for future England coaches to call upon. NRL clubs have oversight of players in several age groups leading up first-grade level.

"The TV deal that the NRL's just signed is enormous and [with that you get] preparation, the facilities and the teams coming through that support each NRL club.

"I don't think Super League clubs could populate three teams underneath them with a genuine six, seven, nine and one [the spine of the team].

"So you end up playing a version of rugby league in the UK at junior level, which is good, it's well coached, it's dedicated and it's full of commitment. But you don't have the genuine six, seven, nine and one influence over a game. This is not a new opinion. This has been going on for a long time.

"If you're asking me, is there a big divide between the competitions? Yeah, there is. It's nothing to do with commitment, nothing to do with good-quality coaching or commitment from players. It's just the size of the competitions and the standing in their country."
